title: How to fix messy textures from tripo/meshy?
author: Top_Measurement7815
selftext:
Anyone knows a good way to fix the messy textures from the models generated by Tripo or Meshy?

I use tripo3d and I tried using their texture edit feature but it's not that good (or I didnt use it right but I spent a good 1 hour trying)

I tried giving the texture base color to gpt image but that doesnt work either

  
Wondering if anyone has a better idea.

comments.author: nicky_factz
comments.body: I’m messing with meshy and Astra in blender, what works fairly well is have gpt part out the model to segments that can be easily attached or fitted to the model, download those, have gpt stitch them and cleanup the quads with blender I was able to produce a fairly good model this way, it’s not perfect but you don’t get these weird artifacts when you don’t try to one shot the whole model in my experiment

comments.author: Nilo_Team
comments.body:
hey hey-

messy textures from tripo/meshy are pretty common- locking the mesh then re-baking usually beats fighting the in-tool texture edit for an hour.

if you're going game-ready, drop poly first (LOD/remesh) so the bake isn't fighting a dense mess, then export GLB.

free browser try with retopo + texture bake + export (no blender): nilo.io - LMK :)

comments.author: meshy_grab
comments.body:
AI 3D generators like Tripo and Meshy are great at producing base shapes, but their textures frequently look blurry, stretched, or "smeary" because of messy autogenerated UV maps and projection artifacts. Feeding flat UV textures directly into ChatGPT or image generators doesn't work because flat UV maps are distorted 2D "unwraps" that 2D image models don't understand.  


Here are the standard workflows developers and 3D artists use to clean them up, ranked from easiest to most control:  


# Method 1: The Blender 3D Projection & Clone Painting Pass (Free & Best Control)

Instead of editing the flat 2D image file, fix the texture directly on the 3D surface in Blender:  


1. **Import model to Blender:** Go to the **Texture Paint** tab.
2. **Use the Clone Stamp Tool:** Select the **Clone Tool**, set a clean area of the model as your source (`Ctrl + Right-Click`), and paint over the blurry or stretched patches.
3. **Use Stencil Projection:** If you have a clean reference photo (e.g., leather, cloth, metal), load it into Blender's Brush Texture settings as a **Stencil**. Overlay the image on top of your 3D view and paint directly through it onto the mesh.
4. **Save Image:** Remember to manually go to `Image > Save` in the Image Editor, or Blender will lose your painted fixes upon closing!

# Method 2: Smart UV Unwrap & Retexture (For Total Cleanup)

If the UV map itself is severely overlapping or stretched, no texture tool will fix it until you fix the UV layout:  


1. Open the model in Blender, enter **Edit Mode** (`Tab`), and select all faces (`A`).
2. Press `U` $\\rightarrow$ **Smart UV Project**. This completely rebuilds the UV islands cleanly without overlaps.
3. Take your clean mesh into dedicated 3D texturing software like **Substance 3D Painter** or free web-based retexturing tools (like 3DAIStudio or Modddif) to generate/paint fresh PBR textures onto the clean UVs.

# Method 3: Using Stable Diffusion / ControlNet (For AI-Driven Fixing)

If you want to keep using AI to sharpen the texture:  


1. Position your 3D model in Blender or a 3D viewport and take orthographic renders/screenshots of the blurry angles.
2. Run those renders through **Stable Diffusion** (or ControlNet with Depth/Normal map control) to generate crisp, high-resolution 2D details.
3. Project those clean renders back onto the 3D model using Blender's **Projection Painting**.

# 💡 Pro-Tip for Workflow Inspection

If you want to quickly inspect the raw geometry, UV maps, and texture files before spending time on a model or committing to export credits, check out **MeshyGrab**.  


It’s a browser extension that extracts raw 3D assets (GLB, OBJ, FBX, STL, 3MF) and texture maps directly from the web preview interface. You can pull the full assets directly into Blender first to inspect the UV layout and see how much cleanup work a model will actually require!
